Stacked bar chart of total ID counts per Condition, split by length range

Source: R/plots.R
plot_bp_count_length.Rd

Plots n_<level> (level one of "Peptides"/"Sequences"/"Proteins") against Condition, filled by Length_range, with a "Total=..." annotation above each bar reporting the "All peptides" row's count.

Usage

plot_bp_count_length(
  df,
  level,
  lim_level,
  shortpep_range = c(8, 13),
  x_var = "Condition",
  palette = NULL
)

Arguments

df

A counts data frame with Condition, Length_range, and an n_<level> column (e.g. the output of count_ids_condition_bylengthrange- style summaries, including an "All peptides" total row per Condition).

level

One of "Peptides", "Sequences", "Proteins" — selects the n_<level> column to plot and labels the y-axis.

lim_level

Upper y-axis limit (e.g. looked up from a count_lim table by Level/"Limit_total").

shortpep_range

Length-2 vector c(min, max) used to label the "others" Length_range class as "< min OR > max AAs".

x_var

Column name for the x-axis (default "Condition"). Pass "Sample" for a per-sample version of the plot.

palette

Optional named character vector mapping Length_range values to fill colours (e.g. c("8 to 13 AAs" = "#fde725", "others" = "#440154")). When NULL (default) scale_fill_viridis_d() is used.

Value

A ggpubr bar chart (ggbarplot) with per-bar count labels, a "Total=..." annotation, and a viridis or manual fill scale.

Details

The original report-inline version closed over three chunk-local globals (count_lim, counts_size_total, shortpep_range); this migrated version threads them through as explicit arguments — lim_level (the y-axis upper limit looked up from count_lim by the caller) and shortpep_range (defaulted to the standard 8-13 AA HLA-I window). The counts_size_total closure reference is replaced by df itself, since every call site already passes counts_size_total as df — these were always the same object.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
plot_bp_count_length(counts_size_total, "Peptides", lim_level = 50000, shortpep_range = c(8, 13))
} # }
